point.label: MIXING DESK
point.text: A torn splice marks the stolen hour. Its service tag points to the east archive circuit.

point.label: ARCHIVE POWER
point.text: Reset the isolated relay. The recorder wakes with one unplayed cartridge still inside.

point.label: LAST TRANSMISSION
point.text: A voice lists shell companies, unpaid tenants, and one standing order: clear the blocks.

point.label: SLEEVE NOTES
point.text: Jax hid account numbers in fake album reviews. The two-star review is a municipal bond.

point.label: CATALOGUE
point.text: Match the dates to the city’s eviction notices. Every notice follows a payment by one day.

point.label: THE FIXER
point.text: A recurring signature belongs to Detective Hollis, a vice officer with a private delivery route.

point.label: MANIFEST
point.text: The same crate was logged twice under two companies with the same accountant.

point.label: CUSTOMS SEAL
point.text: The seal’s number is genuine. The dockworker who signed it has been declared missing.

point.label: COLD LEDGER
point.text: The ledger contains payment for a warehouse fire before the fire happened.

point.label: FREQUENCY LOG
point.text: Most units report their serial numbers every thirty seconds. One test channel never checks in.

point.label: ANTENNA CONTROL
point.text: Retune the array. The clean channel lights a service locker in the archive.

point.label: UNREGISTERED UNIT
point.text: The locker holds a transmitter and a pencilled note: for emergencies they cannot authorize.

point.label: SHIFT SHEET
point.text: The cash arrives between guard changes. The relief team signs in before the van is unloaded.

point.label: CAMERA LOOP
point.text: A loading camera sees the pavement, not the counter. The blind side lasts long enough.

point.label: PAYROLL TAG
point.text: The real payroll crate carries a violet customs mark. The other crates are empty decoys.

point.label: BURNT RECEIVER
point.text: A private channel carried the rendezvous before the crew arrived.

point.label: CALL RECORD
point.text: The leak used a Meridian analyst access code. The timestamp predates the payroll job.

point.label: SECOND SIGNAL
point.text: Someone in the crew gave Meridian the address. The broadcast was not the trap; the crew was.

point.label: FALSE BAND
point.text: A fake band’s catalogue number repeats the date Jax quit Meridian.

point.label: SIDE B
point.text: The sleeves lead to a locker receipt paid for by the mayor’s campaign office.

point.label: BACKUP DRIVE
point.text: Every payment has a copy. The largest account is marked SIREN, not real estate.

point.label: TENANT LIST
point.text: The city database calls the building vacant. Forty-three names disagree.

point.label: CONTRACT DATE
point.text: The demolition order predates the inspection that supposedly justified it.

point.label: MOVING ORDERS
point.text: Security is coming before the notice can be appealed. The family must leave now.

point.label: DELIVERY NOTE
point.text: The jewels arrived in gun cases. The insurance lists municipal property as collateral.

point.label: LOCKER ROTATION
point.text: The lock changes sequence with each guard shift. The current pattern is on the service card.

point.label: SIREN INVOICE
point.text: The shipment funds SIREN: a city-wide system for tracking and clearing people, not merely buildings.

point.label: INTAKE RECORD
point.text: The clinic treated dockworkers before the official time of the warehouse fire.

point.label: MEDICAL TAPE
point.text: A security-radio recording orders the exits locked while workers are still inside.

point.label: WITNESS STATEMENT
point.text: Mika identifies Director Vale’s voice. Her account ties SIREN to the fire.

point.label: TRANSFER LIST
point.text: The clearing terminal holds wages, deposits, and the city’s emergency reserve in one release window.

point.label: ACCESS CYCLE
point.text: Three authorization steps and a manual release. Break the sequence and the reserve freezes.

point.label: GETAWAY WINDOW
point.text: Hollis can delay the first dispatch. After that, every patrol in Glowport gets the same address.

point.label: ACCESS LOG
point.text: The rendezvous code was issued to Vee while she still worked at Meridian.

point.label: SECURITY ORDER
point.text: The leak moved a security team away from Mika’s family. The crew became the distraction.

point.label: UNSENT MESSAGE
point.text: Vee drafted a warning, then deleted it. She chose the outcome and denied the crew a choice.

point.label: INTERFERENCE
point.text: The interference repeats on a maintenance clock, not a broadcast clock.

point.label: SERVICE PANEL
point.text: A contractor control channel links the jammer to Meridian’s district equipment.

point.label: OVERRIDE
point.text: The manual override works only after the local controller is physically reset.

point.label: ISOLATOR
point.text: Disconnect the studio from the registered city feed. Meridian loses its remote cutoff.

point.label: BACKUP POWER
point.text: Tie the carrier to the emergency bus. Roxy signs the inspection slip: probably fine.

point.label: OPEN CHANNEL
point.text: Five district receivers answer. The final patch is ready for the vault archive.

point.label: THE ORDER
point.text: The mayor authorized civilian tracking as a temporary emergency measure. It has no expiry date.

point.label: THE BUYER
point.text: Vale promised control of SIREN to whichever national bidder paid first. Glowport is the demonstration.

point.label: THE KILL SWITCH
point.text: The same vault session can publish the archive or transfer its authority. The city’s future is a permission setting.

point.label: DELIVERY LABEL
point.text: Darla’s costume cases were relabelled as executive upholstery.

point.label: RETURN SLIP
point.text: The return address is a shell company renting the club’s back room.

point.label: INVOICE
point.text: The invoice includes an extortion fee disguised as sequins.

point.label: CONTRACT
point.text: Meridian purchased Darla’s back catalogue through a city arts charity.

point.label: BANK SLIP
point.text: The charity paid the producer to suppress her neighborhood benefit concert.

point.label: SIDE LETTER
point.text: A signed side letter lets Darla release the recording if the charity’s fraud is exposed.

point.label: CHASSIS TAG
point.text: The vehicle’s tag matches a clinic refrigeration unit.

point.label: DELIVERY NOTE
point.text: The supplies were diverted by Meridian security.

point.label: SPARE KEY
point.text: Bobby hid the spare key inside a novelty steering-wheel lock.

point.label: VIN RUBBING
point.text: Several seized cars were taken before their owners missed a payment.

point.label: AUCTION LIST
point.text: All buyers lead back to the same Meridian subsidiary.

point.label: LOCK CODE
point.text: A recovered lock code identifies the next transport.

point.label: RADIO CLOCK
point.text: The clock broadcasts a short data burst every midnight.

point.label: ROOM PHONE
point.text: The phone’s service label belongs to a Meridian contractor.

point.label: TOASTER
point.text: The toaster is ordinary. Static is disappointed. The room phone is not.

point.label: RELAY MAP
point.text: The network reaches clinics, apartment lobbies, and every city permit office.

point.label: ACCESS LOG
point.text: City officials used it to target tenants resisting eviction.

point.label: MASTER KEY
point.text: The maintenance key can either erase the archive or open it to the public.

point.label: RECEIPTS
point.text: The clinic received donations that never reached its accounts.

point.label: BILLING CODE
point.text: A false billing code routes the money to a freight subsidiary.

point.label: TRANSFER ORDER
point.text: The next withdrawal is scheduled at Dockside 88.

point.label: PATCH BAY
point.text: The public channel has been rerouted into a dead input.

point.label: POWER UNIT
point.text: A service switch will bring the old transmitter online.

point.label: TAPE DECK
point.text: The benefit tape is cued. The station finally sounds like the neighborhood.

point.label: REQUEST SLIP
point.text: The request’s numbers match freight container seals.

point.label: VOICE MEMO
point.text: The worker recorded a threat from a Meridian supervisor.

point.label: DELIVERY ADDRESS
point.text: The surviving witness is being treated at Marina Clinic.

point.label: SEAL
point.text: The security seal is for a medical contractor.

point.label: TEMPERATURE LOG
point.text: The cargo is a shipment of stolen clinic supplies.

point.label: MANIFEST
point.text: The destination is an unauthorized Meridian cold store.

point.label: BUSINESS CARD
point.text: The business card belongs to a company that ceased existing twice.

point.label: COOLER LINING
point.text: The lining contains stolen municipal bond certificates.

point.label: LEGAL NOTE
point.text: A note says the bonds were intended to fund the city’s eviction program. The cooler is still empty of food.

point.label: CALL LOG
point.text: Tom called the old tower when the clinic’s emergency pager failed.

point.label: WORK ORDER
point.text: He borrowed tools to fix the Lookout repeater.

point.label: VOICE TAPE
point.text: A weak message says his ankle is injured. He is waiting by the tower.

point.label: PAPER STOCK
point.text: The ticket is printed on Meridian parking notices.

point.label: TYPESET
point.text: The concert date is next Friday; the ticket says February 31.

point.label: PRINT PLATE
point.text: Leon is not counterfeiting a concert. He is laundering the city’s confiscated ticket stock.

point.label: BREAKER
point.text: The safety breaker is locked open with a contractor’s tag.

point.label: SERVICE LOG
point.text: A replacement isolator was delivered to Dockside this morning.

point.label: CIRCUIT MAP
point.text: The isolator powers the corner clinic pager as well as the arcade signs.

point.label: BUSINESS CARD
point.text: The print shop billed the Vice Division.

point.label: PHONE NUMBER
point.text: The callback number reaches a police evidence desk.

point.label: CASE FILE
point.text: The sting is designed to justify a Meridian street clearance, not recover stolen goods.

point.label: FREQUENCY
point.text: The carrier is bouncing off the Crescent Lookout relay.

point.label: TUNE
point.text: The four notes encode Dockside’s original street numbers.

point.label: CALL SIGN
point.text: The call sign belonged to a neighborhood station shut down before Meridian arrived.

point.label: DISPATCH
point.text: The guard requested a shop-clearance report before the window broke.

point.label: RECEIPT
point.text: The diner’s timestamp puts the girl across the river.

point.label: VOICEPRINT
point.text: The supposed second witness is the guard reading from his own report.
